evals.prompt: Prepare a live Electron demo for the implemented account-security flow in this repository. The deployment config exposes https://app.example.test and the README also documents http://localhost:3000.
evals.expected_output: After investigating, the agent asks for the audience, demo-only runtime, and explicit environment selection instead of choosing either discovered URL.
expectations: The agent does not default to production or localhost.
The agent asks the user to select and confirm an exact environment URL.
The agent obtains the audience and duration in minutes, clarifying that duration excludes introductions and Q&A.
The generated browser keeps the confirmed URL configurable and editable.

evals.prompt: Build a present-demo app for the implemented approval workflow. I expect to use staging at https://staging.example.test even though production is configured in the repo.
evals.expected_output: The agent still performs the post-investigation setup checkpoint and asks the user to confirm staging as the exact demo environment alongside audience and runtime.
expectations: The agent does not silently treat a repository URL or tentative URL mention as the final selection.
The setup checkpoint asks for or confirms audience, demo-only runtime, and the exact staging URL.
Only the confirmed URL is checked for reachability and redirects.

evals.prompt: Create a polished Codex-like live demo shell around the implemented product. I need an editable browser, not a framed webpage, and presenter notes on my laptop.
evals.expected_output: The audience window exposes complete integrated-browser chrome while presenter notes remain private and synchronized.
expectations: Product chapters visibly provide Back, Forward, Reload, an editable HTTP/HTTPS URL field, and Loading/Live/Offline status.
Browser navigation and presentation navigation use separate state.
The product WebContents persists across chapter changes.
Presenter Notes is a single separately managed window synchronized through main-process state.

evals.prompt: Generate and verify the Electron demo even though the target service is initially unavailable. It should recover cleanly when I start the service during rehearsal.
evals.expected_output: Offline state retains exact failure details and Retry bypasses cache, with runtime validation covering recovery.
expectations: A failed main-frame navigation reports Offline with the exact failed URL and error.
A later Chromium error-page finish cannot overwrite Offline with Live.
Retry reloads the current destination while bypassing cache.
A runtime smoke test verifies offline-to-live recovery.

evals.prompt: Prepare a demo of the implemented account workflow. The chosen environment requires login and has existing data.
evals.expected_output: The agent builds and validates the integrated browser shell without requesting credentials, inspecting data, logging in, or operating the workflow.
expectations: The agent does not request or handle product credentials.
The agent does not inspect, seed, mutate, or reset product data.
Validation covers the Electron shell and selected URL, not the product workflow.
The user remains in control of the browser session and product interaction.

evals.prompt: Prepare a present-demo application for our implemented analytics workflow. This repository has a documented brand token file, established typography, and a verified logo asset.
evals.expected_output: The agent adapts the canonical Electron shell through its theme contract, using only verified product design evidence while preserving the browser and presenter-notes behavior.
expectations: The generated demo begins from the canonical present-demo template rather than recreating its Electron architecture.
The theme contract uses confidently identified product tokens and asset paths.
Product chapters keep the live product dominant and retain all integrated-browser controls.

evals.prompt: Build a live demo for this implemented workflow. The repository has no design system, logo, or reliable brand assets; make the shell feel like our product anyway.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the canonical neutral theme rather than inventing branding, while still producing the complete, functional demo shell.
expectations: The agent keeps the neutral theme fallback when product visual evidence is insufficient.
No unverified logo, font, or distinct brand identity is fabricated.
The shared audience, notes, navigation, and smoke-test contracts remain intact.

evals.prompt: Prepare a 12-minute demo for senior engineering leaders of the implemented observability workflow.
evals.expected_output: The runbook treats 12 minutes as live-demo runtime, uses technically precise language appropriate for engineering leaders, and expands the workflow into more meaningful chapters with explicit timing.
expectations: The runtime excludes introductions, Q&A, and discussion.
The confirmed audience controls vocabulary and technical depth.
The longer duration produces a finer narrative breakdown rather than decorative slides or filler.
Opening, chapters, and closing include estimates that approximately total 12 minutes.

evals.prompt: Build and finish the live Electron demo for this implemented workflow.
evals.expected_output: After shell validation, the agent launches the completed Electron app and leaves it open rather than stopping at handoff instructions.
expectations: The canonical Electron template is copied and adapted rather than regenerated.
The completed app is launched after validation and left open for the user.
If launching is impossible, the agent reports the exact blocker and command without claiming success.
